entries.title: Claude Sonnet 5 is the new default model (1M context)
entries.paragraph: Claude Sonnet 5 becomes the default model in Claude Code, with a native 1M-token context window and promotional pricing of $2/$10 per million tokens through August 31. Update to 2.1.197 or newer to get access; existing model pins still work if you prefer to stay on your current model.
entries.whyItMatters: The default model just changed under everyone — a fresh install or an unpinned config now runs Sonnet 5 with a much larger context window, which changes both cost and behavior of automated runs.

entries.title: Default permission mode renamed to "Manual"; AskUserQuestion no longer auto-continues
entries.paragraph: The "default" permission mode is now labelled "Manual" across the CLI, --help, VS Code, and JetBrains — --permission-mode manual and "defaultMode": "manual" are accepted alongside the old default. Separately, AskUserQuestion dialogs no longer auto-continue by default; you now opt into an idle timeout via /config. A startup crash when disabledMcpServers/enabledMcpServers is a non-array value was also fixed.
entries.whyItMatters: Unattended flows that relied on AskUserQuestion silently auto-continuing will now block waiting for input unless you configure an idle timeout.

example.code:
# old and new spellings both work
claude --permission-mode default ...
claude --permission-mode manual  ...

entries.title: New OTel event logs the model's response text on upgrade
entries.paragraph: A claude_code.assistant_response OpenTelemetry log event now carries the model's response text. It is redacted unless OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=1, but when that variable is unset it follows OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS — so any deployment that already logs prompt content will start emitting response content the moment it upgrades. This release also adds autoMode.classifyAllShell to route every shell command through the auto-mode classifier.
entries.whyItMatters: If you ship telemetry to a shared backend, upgrading can silently start exporting full model responses — set OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=0 before you roll out.

example.code:
# keep telemetry to prompts-only after upgrading
export OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=0

entries.title: Subagents run in the background by default; Chrome GA; auto-PR on finish
entries.paragraph: Subagents now run in the background by default, so the main session keeps working and is notified when they finish. Claude in Chrome reached general availability. Background agents launched from claude agents now commit, push, and open a draft PR when they finish code work in a worktree instead of stopping to ask, and the built-in Explore agent now inherits the session's model (capped at opus) rather than running on haiku.
entries.whyItMatters: Delegated work parallelises without babysitting, but background agents can now push branches and open PRs on their own — review your worktree and permission setup before running them unattended.

entries.title: requestId on permission callbacks, blocked workflow events, masked credential injection
entries.paragraph: Permission callbacks now receive a requestId so you can correlate a decision back to the exact request that triggered it. Workflow agent events gain a blocked field, and sandboxed commands now support masked credential injection — secrets are made available to a command without appearing in logs or transcripts.
entries.whyItMatters: Correlating permission prompts by requestId removes the guesswork in multi-agent orchestrators, and masked injection lets sandboxed steps use secrets without leaking them.

entries.title: Query.reinitialize() recovers a session after a transport gap
entries.paragraph: A new Query.reinitialize() method re-sends the initialize control request and redelivers any pending permission or dialog prompts after a transport gap. If your SDK host drops and reconnects its channel to the agent, you can now resync state instead of tearing the session down.
entries.whyItMatters: Long-lived SDK sessions behind flaky networks or load balancers can recover in place rather than losing an in-flight permission prompt.

entries.title: Per-server MCP timeouts and shadowed-callback warnings
entries.paragraph: MCP servers can now be given per-server timeout options instead of one global value, and the SDK emits a runtime warning when a callback configuration is shadowed by another. A mapping bug where SDKUserMessage.isSynthetic was not carried through to isMeta on ingestion was also fixed.
entries.whyItMatters: A single slow MCP server no longer forces you to loosen the timeout for every server, and the shadowing warning surfaces config mistakes that used to fail silently.

entries.title: agent_id on permission requests; ReadMcpResourceDirTool; rewind control request
entries.paragraph: Permission requests originating from background agents now carry an agent_id so a host can tell which agent is asking. The release also introduces ReadMcpResourceDirTool as a dedicated tool type and a rewind_conversation control request for programmatically stepping a session back.
entries.whyItMatters: Hosts orchestrating several background agents can now attribute and route each permission prompt to the right agent instead of treating them as one anonymous stream.

entries.title: MCP tools use tool search by default; system-proxy auth on macOS; dark-mode plugin logos
entries.paragraph: Codex now uses tool search by default when an MCP server supports it, improving tool discovery while staying compatible with older models and providers. macOS authentication clients can honour system proxy, PAC, and WPAD settings when respect_system_proxy is enabled, plugins can ship dedicated dark-mode logos via local manifests and remote catalogs, and apps can render richer safety-buffering UI from server-provided metadata.
entries.whyItMatters: Large MCP tool catalogs get discovered by search instead of being dumped into context, and corporate macOS fleets behind a proxy can finally authenticate without manual overrides.

entries.title: Stop full Responses WebSocket payloads leaking into trace logs
entries.paragraph: A fix prevents full Responses WebSocket request payloads from being written to trace logs. Previously, enabling verbose tracing could persist entire request bodies — including their contents — to disk. Backported to the 0.142 release line.
entries.whyItMatters: If you run Codex with tracing on, upgrading stops sensitive request payloads from being captured in log files that may be shipped off-box.

entries.title: Opt-in Windows system proxy support for authentication
entries.paragraph: Codex adds opt-in Windows system proxy support for authentication, covering PAC and WPAD auto-configuration, static proxies, and bypass rules. This mirrors the macOS proxy support landing in the same release train.
entries.whyItMatters: Windows users behind a corporate proxy can now sign in without hand-rolling proxy environment variables.

entries.title: afterCompletion hook for runTools, realtime sideband call_id, stream helpers
entries.paragraph: The runTools helper gains an afterCompletion hook that fires after each tool-calling round, the realtime API adds sideband call_id support, and new response stream helper utilities land. Bug fixes address structured-output parsing and stream abort-listener cleanup.
entries.whyItMatters: The afterCompletion hook gives you a clean place to log, cost-track, or short-circuit a tool-calling loop between rounds instead of wrapping the whole call.

suggestions.title: Audit unattended flows for the Manual-mode + AskUserQuestion behavior change
suggestions.paragraph: Claude Code 2.1.200 renamed the default permission mode to "Manual" and stopped AskUserQuestion dialogs from auto-continuing. Any CI job, cron, or headless script that assumed a question would eventually self-resolve will now hang. Configure an explicit idle timeout via /config, or restructure the flow so it never asks a question in unattended mode.
suggestions.whyItMatters: A silently-blocking prompt in an overnight pipeline looks identical to a hang — you find out when the job never finishes.

example.code:
# both spellings accepted; be explicit in scripts
claude --permission-mode manual -p "..."

suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · 2.1.200 · Jul 3 — Default permission mode renamed to "Manual"; AskUserQuestion no longer auto-continues

suggestions.title: Pin OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=0 before upgrading if you ship telemetry
suggestions.paragraph: The new claude_code.assistant_response OTel event follows OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS when its own flag is unset. If your service already logs prompt content to a shared observability backend, upgrading will start exporting full model responses too. Set OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=0 in the environment before rolling out the new version.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Model responses can contain code, secrets, and customer data — you do not want them landing in a telemetry pipeline by accident.

example.code:
# in your deploy env / Dockerfile
ENV OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=0

suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · 2.1.193 · Jun 25 — New OTel event logs the model's response text on upgrade

suggestions.title: Upgrade Codex to 0.142.5 if you run it with tracing enabled
suggestions.paragraph: Codex 0.142.5 stops full Responses WebSocket request payloads from being written to trace logs. If any of your machines run Codex with verbose tracing on — CI runners, shared dev boxes — those logs may already contain complete request bodies. Upgrade, then rotate anything that may have been captured.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Trace files are routinely shipped to central logging, so a payload leak here can quietly widen the blast radius of a single request.
suggestions.tiesTo: Codex · 0.142.5 · Jul 1 — Stop full Responses WebSocket payloads leaking into trace logs

suggestions.title: Plan a Sonnet 5 migration and lock in the promo pricing window
suggestions.paragraph: Claude Sonnet 5 is now the default with a 1M-token context window and promotional pricing of $2/$10 per Mtok through August 31. If your service pins a model, test Sonnet 5 against your evals now; if it does not pin, be aware that a fresh install already runs Sonnet 5, which changes both cost and long-context behavior. Budget for the price step-up after the promo ends.
suggestions.whyItMatters: A larger default context window quietly raises per-run token cost, and the promo window is a finite chance to benchmark cheaply.
suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · 2.1.197 · Jun 30 — Claude Sonnet 5 is the new default model (1M context)

suggestions.title: Correlate SDK permission decisions with requestId and use masked credential injection
suggestions.paragraph: If your service embeds the Claude Agent SDK, read the new requestId in your canUseTool callback and stamp it onto your audit log so every allow/deny ties back to a concrete request. For sandboxed steps that need a secret, switch to masked credential injection (SDK v0.3.199) so the value is available to the command but never rendered into logs or transcripts.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Auditable, per-request permission decisions and leak-proof secret handling are exactly what a security review of an agent integration will ask for.
suggestions.tiesTo: Claude Agent SDK · v0.3.199 · Jul 2 — requestId on permission callbacks, blocked workflow events, masked credential injection
